title: Network policy granularity and upgrade-safety PRD for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD to define exact networking policy granularity, testable upgrade safety gates, and acceptance criteria for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments in regulated or air-gapped environments. Focus areas: 1) fine-grained egress/ingress policy templates for operators; 2) automated pre-upgrade validation for offline mirrors and proxy configurations; 3) safety nets for KMS/HSM rotations during staged upgrades; and 4) minimal runtime connectivity surface for hardened deployments. This doc consolidates open questions from field engineering and SRE, and defines concrete acceptance criteria, test harnesses, and rollback contracts.
scope_in: Define canonical network policy templates mapped to three customer profiles (open, restricted, zero-egress)
Specification of pre-upgrade validation checks that run locally (no outbound) and via staging mirror when available
Acceptance criteria for operator-run offline image sync and integrity verification
Upgrade safety flows for KMS/HSM rotations (order of operations, timeouts, rollback steps)
Metrics and dashboards required to validate upgrade health (latency, failed requests by route, cache hit ratio)
scope_out: End-to-end automated image distribution via physical media (separate PM request)
New cryptographic protocols for KMS (out of scope; rely on existing KMS integrations)
Changes to hosted API SLA language or pricing
acceptance_criteria: Operators can apply one of three network policy templates (open/restricted/zero-egress) with a single CLI flag or UI toggle
Pre-upgrade validation exits with non-zero status when any required connection (mirror, operator API, local kubelet) is misconfigured; exit codes documented
Offline image sync process verifies signatures and checksums locally and produces an artifacts report; sample report format included
Staged upgrade with KMS rotation completes without dropped TLS connections to dependent services in >=99% of test runs for the Restricted template
Rollbacks can be triggered automatically on stalled upgrade (no progress >15 minutes) and restore previous crypto keys for traffic in <10 minutes in testing harness
Acceptance test suite (described below) passes in both fully connected and mirrored-airgap simulated environments
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests in CI for validation code paths (no network) - required coverage 90% for new modules
End-to-end upgrade lab: three scenarios (connected, mirrored-airgap, zero-egress) run automated nightly; record traces and logs to a dedicated dashboard
Canary rollout simulation using the staging mirror and injected network partitions (chaos) to verify rollback triggers
KMS rotation dry-run: rotate test key in sandbox and assert token validity, secrets unseal, and service reconnection within thresholds
Customer acceptance checklist for on-prem SREs with steps, expected outputs, and troubleshooting commands
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind operator-config flag; enabled for internal pilot accounts only
Week-1: internal pilot (1 cluster) with full observability and on-call coverage
Week-2: pilot expansion (3 clusters) and run simulated airgap upgrades
Week-3: lock down rollback runbooks, document required operator permissions, enable for customer opt-in
General availability once pilot feedback shows <2 rollbacks and no unresolved high-severity issues
risks: Customers have heterogeneous firewall/proxy rules; templated policies may need per-customer adjustments
KMS rotation during upgrade has complex failure modes that could block unseal on some HSMs
Air-gapped mirrors with inconsistent artifact ordering could cause partial upgrades if pre-checks are insufficient
Operator unfamiliarity with new templates may lead to misconfiguration during early rollout
mitigations: Provide a diagnostic CLI that simulates operator environment and emits an actionable report
Require signature-verified artifacts and include a local verification step before applying changes
Add explicit timeout and watchdog that triggers rollback on stalled progress; include operator alerting
Ship step-by-step runbook, example values for common environments, and office-hours support during pilot
